correctness.rationale: Independently counted priority multiplicities by testing every candidate matching rather than simulating priority orders. For an agent receiving object x, every object she prefers to x must have been consumed by its assigned owner first. Thus the orders realizing a matching are exactly the linear extensions of its predecessor constraints; subset DP counts them, giving zero for a cycle. Relabeling objects uniquely normalizes the first agent to the identity ranking and gives weight 24 for each of the remaining 24^3 profiles. All counts are exact, and multiplicities sum to 24 per profile. All 57 shape-frequency rows and 16 support-frequency rows match the two frozen CSVs, as do the impossible sizes, unique normalized full-support profile, mean and tail probability. Replay: python3 /workspace/review_evidence/priority.py.

Its 57 signatures and counts are identical row for row after sorting multiplicities in the same direction. It gives the entire support histogram, forbidden sizes, identical-profile full-support criterion and the same mean; it additionally gives the variance and characterizes support size one. value.rationale: The original small-market census is a useful exact benchmark for lottery concentration, as opposed to a marginal assignment matrix. In this submission it is a recount of the known complete distribution; the exact tail is elementary aggregation of known cells.
